output:
**Written Statement Regarding Complaint Dated October 29**

To: Mrs. Okafor
cc: Darlene [Last Name], Transportation Supervisor; Driver Personnel File

From: [Your Full Name], Driver, Bus 41, Route 9 Elementary
Date: November [__], 2026

Dear Mrs. Okafor,

I was asked to write my account of what happened on the afternoon of Tuesday, October 27, for my file. I was told you will get a copy, so I am writing it to you directly. I want to be respectful and clear about what I saw and why I did what I did. I am not writing this to argue with you. I drive Amara every day, I care about her getting home safe, and I want us to be able to work together from here on.

**What happened that afternoon**

On Tuesday, October 27, I was driving the afternoon run on Bus 41, Route 9 elementary. Amara's stop is at Kessler Avenue and Brandt Street. Amara is in kindergarten at Fairmont Elementary and has the green tag on her backpack. That tag tells the driver an adult has to be at the stop before she can get off the bus.

The schedule has us at Kessler and Brandt at 3:50. I got there at 3:52. I stopped and looked for an adult at the corner and did not see anyone. I waited until about 3:55 and still did not see anyone I could identify as there for Amara.

The district rule for kindergarten riders is that if no adult is at the stop, the student stays on the bus and goes back to the school, and the school office calls the parent. That is what I did. At 3:56 I radioed dispatch, and Gloria at dispatch called Fairmont to let them know Amara was coming back. I still had three more stops and fourteen other children on the bus, so I finished the route and then drove Amara back to the school.

We got to Fairmont at 4:31. I did not just drop her at the door. I walked Amara into the office myself and handed her over to Mrs. Petrakis.

**How Amara was doing**

I want you to know Amara was fine the whole time. She was not upset or crying. She was coloring on her folder, and at one point she asked me if she could ride some more. I told her we were going on a little extra trip. I kept it light so she would not be scared, and she was not.

**Where you were parked**

I understand from the complaint that you were parked across Brandt Street by the laundromat and that you waved to me. I am sorry to say I did not see you. There was a box truck parked on that side of the street that day, and it blocked my view of that side. I was looking at the corner where Amara gets off, and from my seat I could not see anyone there.

I also want to explain why I did not get off the bus to go look across the street. I had fourteen other children on board. I am not allowed to leave a bus full of children to cross the road and look around, and I would not do that even if I were allowed. Their safety is my responsibility the same as Amara's is.

**About the comment that I was laughing**

I was told you said I drove off laughing. I want to answer that respectfully, because I know how that must have looked and felt from where you were. I was not laughing. As we were pulling out, a fourth grader in seat 2 was standing up, and I was telling him to sit back down. Whatever you saw through the window was me talking to that student. I would never laugh at a parent or at a situation like that one.

**Why I followed the rule**

I have been driving school buses for 28 years and have never been written up. In all that time I have tried to do things the right way, and the green tag rule is one I take seriously. A kindergartner cannot be let off at a stop with no adult I can see. It does not matter whether I know the family or how long I have been driving them. If I cannot see the adult, the child stays with me.

This has happened once before on my route, years ago, with a different family. It was hard on them that day too, but afterward they understood why it is done this way. I mention it only to say I have handled this the same way every time, for every child.

**I understand you were scared**

I have grandchildren of my own. If I were sitting in my car watching a bus pull away with one of them on it, I would be scared too, and probably angry. I do not hold that against you at all. I am truly sorry you had such a bad afternoon and that you were worried about Amara for that time.

I will be honest and say I am not going to apologize for following the rule, because it is there to protect Amara and every other little one on my bus. But I am sorry for what that afternoon put you through, and I mean that.

**Request to review the bus camera footage**

Bus 41 has a camera system, and it would have recorded the stop at Kessler and Brandt on October 27. I respectfully ask that the transportation office pull the footage from that afternoon, from when we came up to the stop around 3:52 until we pulled away around 3:56. I believe it will show the corner where Amara gets off, how long I waited, the box truck on the other side of Brandt, and what was going on inside the bus when we pulled out, including the student in seat 2. I am glad to have it reviewed and would like it added to the file with this statement.

**A request going forward**

So this does not happen again, I would like to ask you a favor. When you pick Amara up, could you please stand on the bus side of the street, at the corner where she gets off? If you need to wait in your car, could you step out of the car when you see the bus coming, so I can see you clearly? Even a quick wave from outside the car on my side of the street makes a big difference. Trucks and parked cars block my view more than people realize, and I want to be sure I can always see you so I can let Amara off right away.

If there is ever a day when someone else will be picking her up, it helps to let the school know, so that person can be on the list and I know to look for them.

**Closing**

Amara is a sweet girl, and I am glad to keep driving her. I want this straightened out so she can keep riding with me and you can feel good about it. If you would ever like to talk about the stop or anything else, I am happy to do that, either through Darlene and the transportation office or with a meeting set up through them.

Thank you for taking the time to read this.

Respectfully,

______________________________
[Your Full Name]
Driver, Bus 41, Route 9 Elementary
[Employee ID, if used]
Date: _______________

---

A few things to fill in before you turn it in Friday: your name, Darlene's last name, the date you sign it, and your employee ID if your office uses one. Have Darlene look it over before it goes to Mrs. Okafor, since she knows how the office likes these done.
